$comment: Single source of truth for the order in which repository gates run.
Consumed by scripts/run-gates.mjs, which backs both `make check-gates` /
`make check-everything` and `npm run check:gates` / `npm run check:everything`.
Do not reorder casually: the tiers are ordered cheapest-and-most-selective
first so a bad change fails in seconds rather than after a release build.

tiers.summary: Shape of the change itself. Pure text/JSON, no compiler needed.
Do the declared interfaces and event/trace schemas parse and agree?
Source changed but a committed generated artifact did not.
Rust correctness. Needs cargo, but no build of the contracts.
Measures real build output. Needs a release build first.

gates.why: A malformed contract scaffold is cheaper to catch than anything downstream.
Two paths differing only in case build on macOS and fail on Linux.
Event definitions drive indexing; drift here is a silent data bug.
Catches interface drift before it is baked into generated SDK types.
The trace tooling validates the fixtures other gates rely on.
ABI and SDK type drift are breaking for integrators, not just noisy.
Generated API docs drift silently because nothing imports them.
Schemas and registries are hand-maintained next to generated docs.
Cheapest possible rejection once we are already paying for cargo.
Clippy plus the repo's error-code convention.
Unused dependencies inflate every WASM size budget downstream.
Last, because it is the only gate that measures compiled output.
